subject: Chat sessions dropping amid throttle surge and retry storms
messages:
From: Claire Donovan <claire@clearhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@clearhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:42:00-05:00
Subject: Unexpected surge of 5xx/429 — chat sessions dropping in prod

Olga,

We're seeing a pretty severe issue right now: between 08:20 and 08:40 ET our product experienced a sustained burst of 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood chat endpoint which coincided with large numbers of user sessions dropping mid-conversation. The failures look concentrated on the streaming chat route — clients start a stream, then get closed with a 5xx or an idle disconnect after ~20-30s, then the client retries aggressively which appears to have caused a retry storm.

We attached session traces and a sampling of client logs (clearhealth-session-traces.zip). Impact: about 12% of active sessions dropped in the window, and a handful of mid-session context was lost. This is producing a lot of downstream customer complaints. Can we get immediate triage and a mitigation? We need a temporary workaround plus a timeline for a fix.

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Platform Reliability
ClearHealth

Attachments: clearhealth-session-traces.zip

Claire — thanks for the report and for the traces. I'm escalating immediately and looping in SRE and your account team.

Immediate plan:
- I'll ask SRE for a short-term mitigation (edge rate-limit / soft-429 + connection circuit-breaker) within the hour.
- CS will provide recommended client defaults for retries/keepalive to reduce feedback loops.
- We'll run targeted throttling for your tenant's routes to prevent cross-tenant impact.

Could you paste the client SDK version and the max_retries setting from your logs (Ben, I saw your attachment — anything else you can call out would help)? I'll schedule a 30-min bridge at 09:10 ET unless you need earlier.

— Olga

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge of 5xx/429 — chat sessions dropping in prod

Triage notes (initial):
- Observed an abrupt spike in inbound request rate to ClearHealth's tenant routes at ~08:18 ET. The per-tenant token/connection counters spiked, followed by increased 429s and then 5xx on streaming sessions as worker queues filled.
- Evidence in the traces: many clients opened streaming sessions, then timed out on the client side after ~25s and retried immediately (no jitter), with max_retries often set to 5-6. That produced a multiplier effect — retry storms are a classic feedback loop here.
- Idle-stream disconnects are occurring while KV cache pressure increases due to many partial sessions (we're seeing more partial KV lookups).

Recommended immediate mitigations (minutes):
1) Enable tenant-scoped soft-429 at the edge (return Retry-After 2s) to slow client retries and reduce burst pressure.
2) Apply a per-connection circuit-breaker for long-lived streams (limit active token window per connection).
3) Temporarily lower per-tenant concurrent request limit to reduce queue depth; route ClearHealth to a throttled pool.
4) Ask ClearHealth to reduce client max_retries to 2 and enable exponential backoff with jitter.

I'll prepare infra toggles for 1-3 now (Hannah: can you roll the soft-429 and circuit-breaker to the dedicated pool for CLH?), and will feed metrics to the bridge.

Vivek
Head of Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@clearhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:15:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge of 5xx/429 — chat sessions dropping in prod

Folks — attaching the client logs (client-logs-20261129.txt). We're on SDK v3.2.1 and I confirm max_retries=6 in our client config; keepalive was disabled due to an earlier bug we thought was resolved.

From the logs you can see the retry loop: requests -> 503/429 -> immediate retry -> another 503 -> exponential queueing. We can flip to max_retries=2 quickly, but want to understand what server-side settings you will change so we can coordinate.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior SRE, ClearHealth

Attachments: client-logs-20261129.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Donovan <claire@clearhealth.com>, Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:27:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge of 5xx/429 — chat sessions dropping in prod

Claire / Ben — quick support action we can take from your side (minutes):
1) Set client max_retries = 2.
2) Enable TCP keepalive / SDK keepalive so streams don't spin up unnecessary handshakes.
3) Add small jitter to retry backoff (uniform 100-600ms) and start backoff at 500ms.
4) Increase client idle timeout to 90s to avoid premature client-side disconnects while we stabilize.

I'll run a short regression in staging with those settings and provide a step-by-step guide: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcdefg/incident-runbook (internal).

We will support the change window through 11:30 ET. If you want our engineers on the call for the config flip, we can join.

— Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-29T10:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surge of 5xx/429 — chat sessions dropping in prod

Patch notes / actions applied to ClearHealth dedicated pool at 10:00 ET:
- Tenant soft-429 enabled at edge with Retry-After: 2s.
- Connection-level circuit breaker added: max active token window per connection = 4; new sessions beyond that get a soft-429.
- Concurrent requests reduced by 20% for CLH routing to an intermediate throttled pool.
- Added a short-lived telemetry counter (INFRA-8742) to watch retry loops and idle disconnects.

Expect effect: this should dampen the retry multiplier and reduce queue growth. Please watch the tenant-specific 5xx and 429 rates; I will keep the flags in place while we validate.

Ticket: JIRA INFRA-8742

Date: 2026-11-29T16:10:00-05:00
Subject: Executive update and next steps — ClearHealth incident 11/29

Claire — apologies again for the disruption today. Summary and next steps: 
- What happened: a client-side retry configuration combined with a burst of concurrent streaming sessions produced a retry storm that amplified load on the serving pool, causing elevated 429s and some 5xx streaming disconnects.
- Immediate mitigations applied: tenant-scoped soft-429, connection circuit-breaker, and temporary throttled routing for your tenant (INFRA-8742). ClearHealth team to apply client changes (max_retries=2, keepalive on, add jitter).
- Short-term timeline: we expect error rates to fall within 1-2 hours as flags stabilize; we will monitor and revert if there are regressions.
- Next steps: 1) joint post-mortem runbook by 12/03; 2) follow-up on improvements to streaming backpressure (engineering) and guardrails to detect retry storms earlier (observability).

We will also apply a one-time service credit for the incident — Sean / account will confirm details with Claire. If you'd like a recap call tomorrow at 09:00 ET, we're available.

Sincerely,
Sean Gallagher
VP Sales & Customer Success
Redwood Inference
